html:
The Yaqui, who call themselves Yoeme, are an Indigenous people of the Yaqui River valley in Sonora, north-western Mexico. Their language belongs to the Uto-Aztecan family and is close to that of the Mayo, their southern neighbours.

They farmed the river floodplain and fought off Spanish expeditions in the 1530s and again in the early 1600s. In 1617 they invited Jesuits of the Society of Jesus instead, who gathered them into eight towns that remain the heart of Yaqui life. Their Easter ceremonies and deer dance mix Catholic and older beliefs.

For most of the 1800s and early 1900s the Yaqui fought Mexico to keep their land, in the Yaqui Wars. Under Porfirio Díaz thousands were deported to work on the henequen plantations of Yucatán. Many fled to Arizona, where the Pascua Yaqui Tribe lives today.
